script: They banned phones, then demanded a WhatsApp photo—my boss just got caught.. The manager decided one morning that phones in the office were a distraction, so they banned us all. I walked in, phone in pocket, feeling like the CEO of my own life. A day later, the same manager, eyes red from too many alarms, grabs the landline and screams, "Send me that roster photo on WhatsApp—now!" I freeze. "Can't do that," I say. He looks at me like I am the problem. "Why not? I am not allowed to use my mobile at work," he says, like a rulebook from the '90s. I roll my eyes. "Oh, you can if I need you to," I say, because I am the one who keeps the vibe alive. And boom—the new policy is just a whisper in the break room: no phones, but only if you're not asking for something. The audacity of it all? It's like they're playing a game of "who can pretend they're more productive." (I know, right?)
